Part 14

Glossary

Every term used in this pack, in plain English, merged from the companion documents and sorted alphabetically.

111 terms.

13F
A quarterly public filing listing a US manager's holdings of US-listed shares. Shows long positions only, with a delay.
2 and 20
2% of assets plus 20% of profits. The classic fee; averages are now lower.
Absolute return
Aiming for a positive return regardless of what markets do. The hedge fund goal.
Accredited investor
Someone with enough income or assets to be allowed into a hedge fund. The law assumes they can bear losses.
Activist
A fund that buys a stake then pushes the company to change.
Allocation (conference)
Deciding who gets scarce meeting slots: the bank allocates among its clients; the buy-side desk allocates among its PMs.
Allocator
An institution that decides where to invest large pools of money: a pension fund, endowment or sovereign wealth fund. Hedge funds' customers.
Alpha
Return that comes from skill rather than from the market moving. If the market is up 10% and your fund is up 12% with the same risk, alpha is roughly the extra 2%.
Analyst (buy side)
A researcher inside a fund who supports a PM by studying companies and building models.
AUM, assets under management
The total value of the money a firm manages for investors. The standard measure of size. Not the same as the firm's own revenue or profit.
Basis point (bp)
One hundredth of one percent. 50bp = 0.5%.
Basis trade
Buying a government bond and selling its future, with borrowed money, to capture a tiny price gap. Huge in size, watched by the Fed.
Beta
Return that comes from simply being exposed to the market. A fund with high beta rises and falls with the index.
Broker
In this guide, a sell-side firm (investment bank or brokerage) that executes trades and sells research and access.
Broker vote
A periodic scorecard in which a fund's investors rate each broker's services. Drives how much the fund pays or values each broker.
Broker-sourced versus originated
Meetings arranged by a bank, versus meetings the firm arranges directly with the company [S40][S42].
Business Development versus Capital Development
At Millennium, Business Development recruits PMs; Capital Development raises money from investors. Neither is corporate access.
Buy side
Firms that invest money: hedge funds, asset managers, pension funds. Millennium is buy side.
Callable commitment
Money an investor pledges that the fund can draw later when it has a use for it, as in private equity. Millennium's structure since 2024.
Capital markets day
A company-hosted event where management presents strategy to all analysts and investors at once.
Captive, platform company
A formerly independent firm that now manages money only for Millennium (Jain Global, Albar) or a large multi-team group inside it (Passaic).
Cash hurdle
Performance fees charged only on returns above what cash pays.
Closed period
Under UK and EU market abuse rules, the 30 days before results when senior managers may not deal in their company's shares. Companies also often avoid private investor meetings then.
Commission
The fee a fund pays a broker per trade. Historically it also quietly paid for research and access ("bundling").
Commission sharing arrangement (CSA)
A mechanism where part of trading commission is set aside to pay for research from any provider. Common between 2006 and 2018.
Consumption report
A record of who at the fund used which broker's services, especially company meetings. Feeds the broker vote.
Control room, restricted list, wall-crossing
Compliance's machinery for managing inside information: which names cannot be traded, and who has been formally given confidential information.
Core team
Millennium's label for shared, non-investing functions such as Business Development, Corporate Access, Equity Research Tools and AI [S50].
Corporate access
Arranging contact between investors and the management of listed companies.
Corporate broker
UK-specific: a bank or broker a listed company retains to advise it and manage its relationship with shareholders. Runs the company's roadshow calendar.
Correlation
How much two things move together. Uncorrelated returns are the whole point of a multi-manager fund.
Crowding
Many funds holding the same positions. Dangerous because they all try to sell at once in a shock.
CTA / trend follower
A computer-driven fund that follows price trends in futures.
De-grossing
Cutting both long and short positions to reduce risk, usually fast and under pressure. When many pods do it at once, prices move sharply.
Drawdown
The fall from a peak to a trough in a fund's or PM's value. Millennium is reported to cut a PM's capital at a set drawdown (see chapter 2A).
EMEA
Europe, the Middle East and Africa. The region the London desk serves.
Enterprise Risk
The firm-wide analytics team that measures PM performance, capital use and liquidation cost across all strategies for the Office of the CIO.
Event-driven
Betting on corporate events: mergers, bankruptcies, spin-offs.
Expert network
A firm (GLG, AlphaSights, Third Bridge, Guidepoint) that connects investors with paid industry experts for calls. Adjacent to corporate access, tightly controlled by compliance.
External allocation, managed account
The platform giving its own capital to an outside manager to run under the platform's controls. Millennium runs 32, the most of any platform.
FCA
Financial Conduct Authority, the UK regulator that authorises Millennium Capital Partners LLP and writes the rules on research payments and market abuse.
Federated versus centralised
Whether investment decisions are made by independent teams (federated, Millennium) or shaped by a central process and shared ideas (centralised, Citadel).
Feeder and master fund
Investors put money into a feeder (often in the Cayman Islands), which invests in a master fund that holds the positions.
Five-year liquidity, 5% a quarter
Investors can withdraw 5% of their money each quarter, so a full exit takes about five years. Millennium's terms since 2018.
Form ADV
The registration document a US investment adviser files with the SEC. Public. The best primary source on a private fund manager's size and structure.
FSB
Financial Stability Board, the international body coordinating regulators on systemic risk.
Gate
A cap on how much money can leave a fund per period.
GP / LP
General partner (the manager) and limited partners (the investors).
GP stake, Petershill
A minority share in a fund manager's own business, not its funds. Petershill is Goldman Sachs' unit that buys such stakes; its funds took about half of Millennium's 15% sale.
Gross asset value, RAUM
Total assets before liabilities, including positions bought with borrowed money, as reported to the SEC. Roughly 7.5 to 9 times net assets at Millennium. Not the same as a leverage ratio.
Gross exposure
Longs plus shorts as a share of capital. A pod with 100 long and 100 short on 50 of capital has 400% gross exposure.
Guaranteed package
A signing deal that promises a PM a minimum payout regardless of performance. A feature of the talent war between platforms.
Haircut
The safety cushion a lender demands against collateral in a repo.
Hedge
A position taken to offset a risk. Short B to hedge long A.
Hedge fund
A private investment fund, open only to institutions and wealthy individuals, that can go long and short, use leverage, and charges performance fees.
High-water mark
The rule that a fund only earns performance fees on gains above its previous peak. Stops it charging twice for recovering losses.
Hurdle rate
A minimum return a fund must beat before performance fees apply. Not all funds have one.
Idiosyncratic risk
The part of a stock's return specific to that company after market, sector and style factors are removed. The only risk a pod is paid to take.
Inducement
Regulatory term for a benefit a broker gives a fund that could bias its behaviour. MiFID II restricts what counts as acceptable.
Inside information / MNPI
Precise, non-public, price-sensitive information. Trading on it is a crime. Corporate access must never be a channel for it.
Investor Relations (IR)
The team inside a listed company that communicates with shareholders and analysts. The desk's main external counterparty on the company side.
IP, investment professional
Millennium's term for PMs and analysts, the desk's internal clients.
Leverage
Borrowing, or using derivatives, to hold positions bigger than your capital. Amplifies both gains and losses.
Limited partner (LP) / general partner (GP)
LPs are the investors in a fund; the GP is the manager that runs it. Millennium Management is the GP; pension funds are LPs.
Lock-up
A period during which an investor cannot withdraw money. Millennium moved most investors to multi-year terms (chapter 2A).
Long / short
Long = own a share, profit if it rises. Short = borrow and sell a share, profit if it falls.
Long-only
A manager that only buys. Most traditional asset managers.
Long-only manager
An asset manager (BlackRock, Fidelity) that only buys, rarely shorts, and is judged against an index.
Loss carry-forward
A PM who loses must earn the loss back before any performance pay; salary is an advance against future profit share.
Macro
Betting on countries: rates, currencies, bonds, commodities.
MAR, Market Abuse Regulation
The UK and EU law defining inside information, insider dealing and unlawful disclosure.
Market neutral
A portfolio built so that market moves roughly cancel out, leaving only the return from stock selection.
MiFID II
EU rules effective 3 January 2018 that, among much else, forced funds to pay for research and corporate access separately from trading.
MNPI / inside information
Material non-public information. Receiving it in a meeting restricts what the recipient may trade; under UK MAR it applies to anyone who receives it [S21].
Multi-manager / multi-strategy / pod shop / platform
A hedge fund made of many independent PM teams (pods) under one risk and capital framework. Millennium, Citadel, Point72, Balyasny.
Multi-manager platform, pod shop
A hedge fund made of many small, separate teams sharing one balance sheet, one risk department and one back office. Millennium, Citadel, Point72 and Balyasny are the big four.
Net exposure
Longs minus shorts. Near zero means market neutral.
Netting risk
The platform pays winning pods a share of their profit even in a year when losing pods drag the total down. The firm bears the gap.
Non-deal roadshow (NDR)
Management tours investor offices when no capital is being raised. Usually broker-organised.
Office of the CIO
The committee created in 2022 that allocates capital and oversees asset-class risk across pods; five members, two of them risk heads.
Origination
The buy-side firm sourcing meetings directly from companies rather than through a broker.
Pass-through
Investors pay the fund's actual operating costs plus a performance fee, instead of a fixed management fee.
Pass-through fees
A fee model where investors pay the fund's actual operating costs (pay, technology, offices) plus a performance fee, instead of a flat management fee.
Payment optionality
The UK's 2024 rule change letting fund managers once again pay for research bundled with trading commissions, subject to guardrails. See chapter 6A.
Performance fee
A share of profits (often 20%) paid to the manager.
PM
Portfolio manager. Runs a book, paid on its profit.
Pod
A PM plus their analysts, running an independent book inside a platform.
Portfolio manager (PM)
The person who decides what a book buys and sells and is paid on its profit.
Prime broker
A bank that lends a hedge fund money and securities, holds its assets and clears its trades. The source of leverage.
PS14/7
The FCA policy statement of May 2014 that, from 2 June 2014, stopped UK managers paying for corporate access with dealing commission [S2].
PSEM / Platform Solutions
Platform Solutions Execution Management, the Execution Services initiative that resources investment professionals "across access, data, research, and technology" [S42]. Siblings: Sector Specialists, Corporate Access, Broker Relations, Content Solutions [S48].
Quant / systematic
Trading decided by models and data rather than human judgement.
Quiet period
A company's self-imposed silence before results, often two to four weeks. Wider than the legal closed period.
Regulation FD
US rule (2000) that a company must publish any material information it gives privately to investors or analysts.
Relative return
Aiming to beat an index. The asset-manager goal.
Relative value / arbitrage
Exploiting small price gaps between related instruments, usually with leverage.
Repo
Selling a bond and agreeing to buy it back: a secured loan.
Research payment account (RPA)
A client-funded pot, created under MiFID II, from which a fund pays for research.
Restricted list
Compliance's list of companies employees may not trade or discuss, often because the firm holds inside information.
Sell side
Investment banks and brokers who sell trading, research and access to investors.
Sell-side
Banks and brokers. They host most conferences and allocate scarce one-on-one slots among their clients [S30].
Sharpe ratio
Return per unit of risk. A Sharpe of 2 is excellent; multi-manager funds target high Sharpe rather than high raw return.
Site visit / field trip
Investors visiting a company's plant, store or HQ.
SMA
Separately managed account: an investor's own account run by the manager, giving full sight of positions.
Soft dollars
US term for paying for research with trading commissions rather than cash.
The centre, Core Infrastructure
Everyone who is not a pod: risk, technology, operations, treasury, compliance, legal, finance, people, execution services, investor relations. At Millennium, 54% of staff.
Trading Services, Business Management
The connective roles that plug a new team into risk, technology, operations, compliance, legal and HR, and that track cost and headcount across the centre.
Unbundling
Separating payment for research and access from payment for trading. The core of MiFID II's research rules.
Volatility
How much returns swing. Lower is calmer.
Wall-crossing
Formally telling an investor inside information (usually about a deal) after they agree to be restricted from trading. Refusing to be wall-crossed is not a defence if you receive the information anyway.
Webex
Cisco's video meeting software, used for your interview. Test it beforehand.

@@p16@@
Part 16

Gaps and open questions

What could not be verified, what is inferred, and what to find out in the interview itself. Read this before quoting any number as fact.

@@c16A@@
Chapter 16A

Gaps and open questions

What could not be verified, what was tried, and how to handle each gap in the interview. An honest gap is safer than a confident guess.

16.1 Research limits

The web-search budget for this session was exhausted part-way through several workstreams; later work relied on direct fetches of known pages. LinkedIn returned an authentication wall on every route; Glassdoor, Wall Street Oasis, Reddit and Blind blocked automated access, so candidate anecdotes come from search-engine snippets only. Bloomberg, FT and CNBC originals were paywalled; their content was read via Hedgeweek, Reuters, Yahoo Finance and other syndications, and headlines were recorded where nothing else could be read. The Internet Archive was unreachable. The FCA Register renders as a JavaScript shell and could not be searched for individuals.

16.2 About the team and the interviewers

Not establishedWhat was triedHow to handle it
Name of the head of the London or EMEA Corporate Access Services deskLinkedIn searches, TheOrg, aggregators, Millennium postings. Only Associates surfaced for London; the "International" head is US-based per aggregatorsDo not guess. If asked who runs the desk, say you found the structure but not the London lead
The Americas head of Corporate Access Services (postings say "heads", plural)SameNot needed on Monday
Direct reporting line from the desk to PSEM leadership and to Execution ServicesInferred from posting language onlySay "sits within Execution Services and Platform Solutions per the postings"
London team headcount; London firm headcountCompanies House accounts give UK-entity totals (423 employees at the LLP; about 1,100 at the employing company) but not team sizeUse the 3 to 6 person range with the method shown in section 1.12
Full career histories, tenure and education for both interviewersLinkedIn login wall; aggregators emptyIrrelevant to the conversation. Do not raise anything you read
Oliver Harvey's exact current title ("Associate, Corporate Access" versus a snippet saying "Junior Trader")Five search variants, TheOrg, reader proxyTreat as a desk practitioner; listen to his self-introduction
Eve Mallabar's role beyond the invitationSearches; nothing publicRole per invitation; process questions to her by email
Any Millennium corporate access staff speaking at IR Society, IR Magazine, NIRI or AIMA eventsAgenda searchesConsistent with a low-profile culture

Not establishedWhat was triedHow to handle it

Millennium's monthly returns for March to May 2026 from a credible outletHedgeweek's Q1 piece omits Millennium; one editorial site claimed about $1.5bn of March losses without sourcesUse +10.5% for the first half, -2.1% July, flat August, +8.2% to end-August
What finally happened to the BlackRock talks (Nov 2024 to mid-2025)BlackRock is absent from every report of the Nov 2025 buyers; one unsourced blog claims talks continued"The reported BlackRock talks did not result in a BlackRock stake; the stake went to Petershill and clients"

Year-by-year returns 2019 to 2023 from pressTaken from a third-party fund database; share class unknownTreat as approximate

Any 2026 regulatory enforcement against MillenniumSearched FCA and SEC with Millennium 2026None found

16.5 About the interview process

Not establishedWhat was triedHow to handle it
Any first-hand account of a Millennium corporate access or business-services interviewGlassdoor, WSO, Reddit, Blind all blocked; snippets onlyThe question bank is built from the JD, regulator texts and peer postings, and is labelled inferred
Programme length and dates for 2027 LondonNot on mlp.com; third parties say about ten weeks from JuneAsk
Whether the CCAT was the assessment for this roleThree prep sites say Criteria Corp for most rolesReconcile with what you actually sat
Rounds after Round 1 for this seat; return-offer rateInferred from other non-investing seats; a "60 to 70%" figure is unsourcedAsk about next steps at the end
How to use a gap in the room

"I could not find X publicly, so I would rather ask than assume" is a good sentence. It shows you researched, know the limits of public information about a private firm, and will not bluff. That is the trait a corporate access desk hires for.

16.6 Added after Round 1 and the 17 September sweep

GapWhat is knownWhat to do
Who Joe and Chris areYou were told at the end of Round 1 that Round 2 is two one-hour interviews with Joe, a member of the team, and Chris, the Head of the Desk. No public professional profile could be matched to either with confidence; the London desk's head is not named in any Millennium posting or filing that was read, and name matches found elsewhere were excluded as unverifiable [S420][S423]. This pack claims nothing about them.Ask the recruiter for full names and titles when the invitation arrives, then check only public professional pages. Adapt live from the first three minutes (chapter 10B).
REQ-30221The recruiter's email cites REQ-30221; the public posting is still REQ-30183 and unchanged since 27 July [S418]. REQ-30221 appears nowhere public.Treat as the internal requisition for the hire. Do not mention it.
The Round 2 formatTwo one-hour interviews is what you were told. How each hour runs (Part 9, chapter 9D; Part 10, chapter 10B) is inference from that, from the Round 1 questions and from the postings.Prepare for both lenses; expect overlap.
Assets under managementMillennium's site says $92bn+ [S71]; Bloomberg reported about $97bn on 7 September [S400]; the pack's earlier chapters carry $89bn to $92bn from July and early September. All are estimates or point-in-time figures.Quote a range with a date: "over $90bn on the firm's own site, nearer $97bn in Bloomberg's September reporting".
The S&P 500 comparisonHedgeweek put the index at about +12% for the year at end-August [S402]; an earlier sweep recorded about +19% at 4 September from a different source [S249]. The two cannot both be right on the same basis; the difference may be total return versus price, or the date.Say "the market is up well into double digits" rather than a number, or cite Hedgeweek with its date.
Pod loss thresholdsThe 5% and 7.5% figures are press-reported and repeated, including in the 7 September Bloomberg feature; Millennium has never published them [S104][S113][S400].Say "reported" every time.
Jain Global's numbersThe gross profit and net figures are a single press report [S407].Use the direction (gross-to-net gap; now captive), not the decimals.
The desk's allocation rule and criteriaNot public. Ollie's remark that broker events are often one seat per firm is the only first-hand detail on the constraint; the desk's ranking criteria are unknown.Never invent a rule. Describe the properties a rule must have (predictable, explainable to the loser, recorded) and say you would learn the desk's.
Programme length and conversion rateNot on mlp.com; third parties say about ten weeks from June, and the firm states it aims to hire its analyst class from the internship [S261][S265].Ask at the end of the second hour.
Research limits, restated

Bloomberg and Financial Times originals were paywalled throughout; where a syndicated copy or a Hedgeweek summary was read, the source table says so. Glassdoor and Wall Street Oasis anecdotes are tagged Low and used only for process shape. Nothing in this pack about Katherine Hayes, Oliver Harvey, Eve Mallabar or Jessica Cresswell goes beyond their public professional roles.
